newsitem.title: EGYPT: Refugees on Egypt-Libya border face hard winter.
newsitem.headline: Refugees on Egypt-Libya border face hard winter.

text.p: The international medical charity Medecins sans Frontieres said on Wednesday that 271 Palestinians stranded at an Egyptian-Libyan border were living in "inhuman conditions" and could not stand another winter.
"The security situation in the camp has worsened. There are cases of harassment of refugees by Libyan security forces, sudden arrests of refugees.." an MSF (Doctors without Frontiers) statement said.
"The psychological state of the refugees is bad and they live in profound despair," the statement sent to Reuters said.
"Space for living is scarce...The tents are in poor condition, as a result of a full year of continuous use: holes, torn down, they will obviously not stand another winter."
The refugees had been living in "inhuman conditions", the statement said.
They were among the thousands of Palestinians expelled by Libya last year in an attempt to show the world that Palestinian self-rule offered nothing to Palestinians in exile.

Most of the deportees went on to other countries but Egypt has refused to let in those without proof that they can leave the country by another border. Israel controls access to the autonomous West Bank and Gaza Strip.
MSF said Libyan security forces had set up a checkpoint about 10 metres (yards) from the border, making the refugees "de facto" on Libyan territory.
MSF said the camp's population had risen to 271 from 200 recently. Many of the new arrivals were visiting family members, university students, and new refugees.
"Hygiene in the camp is poor. The refugees live on a garbage field," MSF said.

The charity said 74 children in the camp were not attending school for the second year and some refugees including six pregnant women needed medical attention. But there appeared to be no malnutrition and quantities of drugs were sufficient.
MSF said it would coordinate with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to visit the camp once every two weeks as well as buy new tents.
